title: Evidence
description: A source-backed claim. Evidence is what separates this product from a blog: every consequential fact points at a page, a date and a verification state. 'Not recorded' is never the same as 'not required'.

sourcePage.description: The human-readable page, when sourceUrl is a PDF or API response.

publisher.description: Who is responsible for the rule — the institution, ministry, agency or portal. Not the aggregator that repeated it.

publisherType.description: Aggregators help discovery but must not be the final authority for an admissions rule.

excerpt.description: A short faithful quotation, or a structured restatement. Keeping the official wording lets a counsellor audit our interpretation.

claim.description: What we take the source to establish, in one plain sentence.

supports.description: Which record and field this evidence backs. Lets the freshness report find every claim that depends on a changed page.

field.description: Dotted path within that record, e.g. requirements[2].threshold.

verifiedBy.description: Who confirmed it. 'automated' is allowed, but not for a consequential rule.

role.description: 'claim' (the default) backs a specific published statement. 'reference' is a page consulted while building a record — an admissions hub, a key-figures report — which has no single sentence to match. A reference is still checked: it must stay live and stay about the same institution. The distinction exists so that citing background reading does not require inventing a claim to justify it.

sourceCheck.description: The result of re-opening the source and looking for the claim. NOT sign-off: this is produced by scripts/verify-evidence.mjs, and verificationState only becomes 'verified' when a person reads the excerpt and agrees. Its value is that it puts the supporting wording next to the claim, which turns review from a research task into a reading task.

outcome.description: supported: every consequential part was found. partial: some was, or the source cannot be read automatically. unsupported: nothing was found, or the page is gone.

claims.description: One entry per claim this record backs, since a single page often supports several.

decisive.description: Whether this claim sets the record's outcome. Entry requirements do; a paraphrased description does not.

weak.description: Matched across a table layout rather than in a single phrase, so the excerpt is worth a closer read.

conflictsWith.description: Other Evidence making an incompatible claim. A conflict downgrades the public result to Needs review; it must never silently resolve to the more permissive reading.

interpretation.description: Why we read the source this way, especially where it is ambiguous or contradicts another official page.
